name: CV / Resume Analysis - UX Designer
description: Extraction rules and signal mappings for UX Designer CVs/resumes. NOTE: Specific evidence mappings (maps_to composite keys) are stored within individual skill files under evidence.cv, NOT here. This file governs section-level extraction rules and signal quality indicators used by the scoring engine.

quality_indicators: Measurable behavioral impact (e.g., 'applied Fogg B=MAP to redesign onboarding, increasing D7 retention by 23%')
Named behavioral frameworks applied in context (Hook Model, CREATE Action Funnel, Dual Process Theory)
A/B test results quantifying UX impact (e.g., 'designed loss aversion CTA that increased conversion 18% in A/B test')
Specific tools used in professional context (Figma, Adobe XD, BPMN modeling tools)
Cross-functional collaboration on behavior change interventions (product, engineering, data science)
Leadership of behavioral design workshops or design sprints
Links to public Figma files, case study portfolios, or design system documentation
Described behavioral design rationale (why a specific intervention was chosen)
Demonstrated full design process from research to prototype to test
Gamification, habit design, or persuasive pattern systems with documented outcomes
Customer journey maps, experience maps, or BPMN diagrams included or linked

portfolio.notes: UX portfolios are the strongest CV-equivalent for practitioners. A portfolio link with case studies demonstrating behavioral design process is weighted higher than work experience descriptions alone.
quality_indicators: Case studies with clear problem statement → research → behavioral diagnosis → intervention → measurement structure
Process artifacts (personas, journey maps, wireframes, prototypes) visible in case study

skills_list.notes: Listing tools (Figma, Sketch) or framework names (Hook Model, BPMN) without project context receives low strength. Must be corroborated by portfolio or work experience.

recognized_certifications: Interaction Design Foundation (IDF) — UX Design, Human-Computer Interaction
BJ Fogg's Tiny Habits Coach Certification

patterns.pattern: Applied Fogg Behavior Model (B=MAP), Hook Model, or CREATE Action Funnel in design process
Designed habit-forming products, engagement loops, or retention mechanics
Conducted user research, created behavioral personas, or ran Jobs-to-be-Done interviews
Created wireframes, prototypes, or high-fidelity mockups in Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD
Produced customer journey maps, experience maps, or service blueprints
Created BPMN process models or EPC diagrams for enterprise workflows
Applied social proof, loss aversion, authority signals, or urgency patterns in product design
Designed and ran A/B tests, analyzed results, and shipped data-driven design iterations
Applied defaults, opt-out patterns, or choice architecture in product design
Used Business Model Canvas, Lean Canvas, SWOT, or competitor analysis in product discovery

important_notes: UX portfolios are significantly stronger evidence than CV descriptions alone — always request and evaluate portfolio link if mentioned
Behavioral framework application must be described in context (what problem, what outcome) — listing 'Fogg Behavior Model' in skills list without application context is low strength
A/B test claims require quantified outcomes (lift percentage, confidence level) to receive high strength
Figma proficiency is effectively table stakes for modern UX designers — depth of component architecture and design system work matters more than tool listing alone
Cross-functional impact (influencing engineering and product decisions with behavioral evidence) is a strong senior signal
